SCHTEACH.TITLE: Intro to Mechanical Eng
SCHTEACH.PEDINN: Introduced an ethical analysis for project II, which involves a literature review over research topic in mechanical engineering.  Students had to perform literature review on selected topic and conclude with future outlook in the field and ethical dilemmas associated with the field.
SCHTEACH.TECHMAT:
Incorporated two AI assignments in the course to expand students' knowledge of the engineering design process.
1. AI Critique: Students were asked to think of an engineering design problem and ask AI to use the engineering design process to solve the problem making in the discrete steps. Students were asked to critique AIs approach and utilization of the process. For example, "Did AI leave out any constraints? Can you think of a better way to test?".
2. AI Interview: Students were asked to conduct an interview with AI about the engineering design process by asking five questions. Students were encouraged to ask deep questions to learn more about the steps and utilization of the engineering process.

SCHTEACH.TITLE: Intro to Mechanical Eng
SCHTEACH.PEDINN: ​Brought in 3D printing and ​SolidWorks components to project.
SCHTEACH.TECHMAT:
For Spring 2024, I created a rubric for the design project. The rubric is based on the Engineering Design Process and was created to help students understand and apply the engineering design process through a design project.

I also incorporated an engineering design challenge, where students had to design an air propelled rocket. I showed the students how to craft their own rocket bodies and allowed them to 3D print rocket components in the Makerspace. Students were introduced to YouTube videos that were crafted for this project and covered easy SolidWorks tutorials and how to convert solid work files to 3D print.

SERVICE_PUBLIC.ORG: Texas Alliance for Minorities in Engineering
CONTENT_GOAL: GOAL 17: Partnerships to achieve the Goal
SERVICE_PUBLIC.DESC: I am volunteering as the Rio Grande Valley Chair for the Texas Alliance for Minorities in Engineering. I have done this since 2016
SERVICE_PUBLIC.ACCOMPLISH:
TAME programs connect Texas students to opportunities in Engineering. When students engage in a TAME Club or participate in a Regional Competition, it doesn’t matter if they’re from a small border town or a city center: they all have access to the same high-quality, engineering education to spark their curiosity.
The world greatly needs the solutions and innovations that a more representative group of engineers would offer, and that’s why TAME is focused on supporting the potential of girls and students from Black, Hispanic, and Native American communities to pursue their engineering dreams.
TAME combines research-based engineering learning opportunities with intentional efforts to build a strong sense of belonging and community among TAME students in the engineering classroom.
TAME recognizes that kids come from very different places, and our programs are designed to meet them where they are.
Taken from ​www.tame.org
